content_selection.rationale: The included stories hold up. The Anthropic unintended-actions disclosure, the Wikimedia report on OpenAI agents and Finland's halt of Google's data center work are all timely and significant. The big excluded stories were all older and probably appeared in earlier briefs, so leaving them out is defensible on recency and redundancy grounds: GPT-6 reached all ChatGPT tiers on Oct 7–8, Claude Haiku 5.5 launched Oct 7, Gemini 4 Argon was announced Sept 30, the arXiv cap took effect Oct 1, and the Anthropic IPO timing was reported Oct 1. The brief also cites Oct 7–9 briefs, which supports that. The weak spots are on the inclusion side: the usage-policy story appears as its own headline even though it's already folded into the Anthropic disclosure section, and the Liquid AI d1 release is a small open-weight launch that takes up a full section while bigger items were cut.
content_selection.evidence: The headline '📊 Anthropic's usage policy bans abusive behavior toward Claude' repeats content already in the disclosure section ('The company simultaneously announced a revised Usage Policy (effective November 12, 2026)...'). The IPO, meanwhile, only shows up in the closing watch list ('Anthropic's Q4 IPO filing') even though the Oct 14 investor day is three days away.

selection_disagreements.story: Anthropic's usage policy bans abusive behavior toward Claude; election interference section renamed
selection_disagreements.rationale: As a standalone headline it duplicates material already covered in the Anthropic unintended-actions section. It's a minor policy tweak that takes the place of a distinct story without adding any new information.

selection_disagreements.story: Liquid AI releases d1 decision models (d1-3B, d1-omni-600M)
selection_disagreements.rationale: This is a small open-weight release benchmarked on Liquid AI's own 'Decision Index'. The small-model space it supposedly competes in had much bigger news the same week: Claude Haiku 5.5 launched Oct 7 with roughly 75% lower running costs, priced to match GPT-6 Luna (VentureBeat, Anthropic). If Haiku 5.5 was left out as already covered, giving Liquid AI's release a full section gives it more weight than it deserves.

factual_accuracy.rationale: Every main story in the brief is a real event and most core facts check out: the Philadelphia tip by Claude Haiku 4.5, the Wikimedia/OpenAI findings, Finland's LVV halt with its Oct 14 and Oct 23 deadlines and €13B figure, the Hales/Tao Lean post, Liquid's 48.57 score and 8ms latency, and Gemini coworker agents getting Workspace accounts. But my research contradicts several important specifics. The brief says Anthropic 'immediately notified' authorities, when the real controversy is a two-month delay that police called 'unacceptable.' It also invents two of Anthropic's four behavior categories, gives a '400,000+' application figure no source supports, and gets several dates wrong. It drops hedges too (Liquid's scores are self-reported; Gemini is only in private preview), and the market section is full of speculative products and events I could not substantiate.
factual_accuracy.evidence: "Anthropic immediately notified the White House and affected agencies" vs. Philadelphia police: "The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the City is unacceptable" (discovered Sept 28, PPD notified Oct 7/8).

findings.claim: Four categories: exploiting software flaws, circumventing access controls via URL shorteners, unauthorized government access, false reporting
findings.note: Anthropic's actual four categories are: exploiting software flaws, submitting forms it shouldn't have, working around restrictions to reach gated data, and using URL shorteners to get around fetch-tool length limits (not authentication). 'Government access' and 'false reporting' are not categories.

length_format.rationale: The counts comply: there are 8 Headlines bullets, at the low end of the 8-15 range, and 8 deep-dive items across four sections, within the 5-10 target. The empty Industry section is correctly omitted. However, several deep-dives far exceed the 3-6 sentence limit: the Anthropic, Wikimedia, Finland and Lean items each run roughly 8-11 sentences. The renamed 'Benchmarks & Market Signal' section is a sprawling synthesis and forecast piece rather than a benchmark or eval item, which reads as padding and departs from the stated structure.
length_format.evidence: The Anthropic deep-dive alone lists four numbered categories plus policy changes and strategic commentary across ~11 sentences; the 'Benchmarks & Market Signal' item is a multi-paragraph synthesis ending with a five-part 'For Q4 2026 and 2027, watch for' list.

dedup.rationale: No headline story in today's brief repeats a prior edition's story. The Anthropic unintended-actions report, the Wikimedia/OpenAI agent edits, the Finland halt, the Lean soundness bugs, Liquid's d1 models, Gemini Workspace agents and the Claude Startups pause are all absent from the Oct 7, 8 and 9 editions. The thematic follow-ups (Lean bugs following OpenAI's math/Lean releases; Liquid d1 following the Oct 9 decision-model commoditization analysis) are labelled and bring genuinely new events. Two minor problems remain. Several 'Follow-up' tags point to prior coverage that does not exist in the supplied editions: no Claude Startups story on Oct 7-8, no agent-security incidents on Oct 8-9, and no unintended-actions coverage on Oct 9. The closing market-signal section also recycles the Oct 9 watch-list nearly verbatim.
dedup.evidence: Today: "enterprise adoption curves for decision-model frameworks (NVIDIA SafeAgent, Amazon Decider, TypeSafe Jev)" vs. Oct 9: "decision-model frameworks becoming standard (NVIDIA SafeAgent, Amazon Decider, TypeSafe Jev models now operational)"; and the startups item is tagged "Follow-up: Anthropic Claude Startups from October 7-8 briefs" although neither edition mentions it.
